Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] Untested theorycraft: nobody publishes this build for 3.2.0, and nobody publishes any Necromancer build for 3.2.0 at all. The argument is narrow and mechanical. 3.2.0's only real gift to Necromancer is the core-stat scalar going from 1.25 to 1.625, a flat 30% on baseline damage per 10 Intelligence. A scalar buff is worth most to the build that can actually spend its affix budget on the core stat - and the class's meta build cannot, because Blood Wave as a Core skill is resource-hungry enough that its published gearing is dominated by Essence Regeneration, Resource Cost Reduction and Lucky Hit restore tempers. Blood Lance is already in that build, as the Overpower-stack spender, and it is not the thing eating the resource budget. This page asks what happens if it is promoted from spender to carry. There is one piece of outside evidence, and it is Season 14 rather than 3.2.0: InfinityBuilds' 2026-08-02 list carries a Blood Lance Necromancer in A tier, titled 'Core Blood Tide Pit 139/Tower 134'. That is a real person clearing real content with the archetype on the live patch - it is not evidence about 3.2.0 and it is not a build guide this page could read, because the site's build pages are JavaScript-rendered.

Rotation
  1. Blood Lance held down as the main cast, Blood Wave on the Overpower cycle, Sever and Blood Mist to move, Bone Prison on anything tanky.
  2. Open on a small pull to build Resolve before engaging anything large.
Variants

Leveling — [ptr] Blood Lance from range as the main cast, Blood Wave when Overpower needs regaining, Sever and Blood Mist to move, Bone Prison on anything tanky. Watch Essence: the whole hypothesis is that this bar does not drain it the way the meta bar does.
Move on when [ptr] Level 70 and Torment 1 - or, on the PTR, whenever Mrak hands them to you - and a first Essence-per-second reading taken.

Early Endgame — [ptr] Blood Lance held down, Blood Wave on the Overpower cycle, everything else as before. This is where the two measurements get taken: Essence per second, and damage before and after stacking Intelligence.
Move on when [ptr] Essence measurably cheaper than the meta bar and Intelligence visibly converting. If either fails, stop.

Late Endgame — [ptr] Unchanged. Run the head-to-head against necromancer-meta-blood-wave here.
Move on when [ptr] The head-to-head is done and this build is at least competitive on packs.

Pushing — [ptr] Untested at push tiers by definition, and doubly provisional because it is PTR data. Open on a small pull to build Resolve before engaging anything large. Both 3.2.0 class tier reads still put Necromancer at the bottom of the game, so a good result here would be surprising and should be double-checked before it is believed.

Uniques
  • pants [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: gamble pants, or target-farm Andariel (Hanged Man's Hall east of Tarsarak, Kehjistan; 1x Greater Lair Key). Carried here on much weaker grounds than in the meta build - it doubles Blood Wave's wave, and this build barely casts Blood Wave. It is the first slot to re-examine. Where →
  • ring 1 [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: Mythic Unique from any lair boss, or one of 3.2.0's three reworked Mythic crafting routes - the Jeweler rune route lets you choose the slot and carries no Crafted tag. Where →

[ptr] Provenance, stated plainly. No 3.2.0 skill tree is published for any build of this class anywhere: the official notes carry no allocations, and Maxroll, Icy Veins, d4builds and d4guides were all still serving Season 14 guides when the PTR digest was written. InfinityBuilds now carries Season 15 PTR builds, but only Warlock ones. This allocation is therefore the specialist's, built from the skill list knowledge/ptr/season-15.md authorises for this class plus the 3.2.0 changes that actually apply. Treat the point counts as a starting shape to test, not as a published build.

Skill point priority

  1. [ptr] Blood Lance first and maxed - the inversion this build is named for
  2. Blood Wave kept low on the bar as the Overpower regain, which is the mirror image of the meta build's arrangement
  3. Bone Prison for attack speed
  4. Sever, Blood Mist and Reap for movement, corpses and Essence
  5. [ptr] Intelligence over Essence Regeneration wherever they compete - that is the entire gearing thesis and it should be visible from the first endgame piece

Board & glyph focus

[ptr] Bloodbath and Dominate come first because the Overpower loop is still the multiplier engine even with the skills swapped round. Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] Untested theorycraft: nobody publishes this build for 3.2.0, and nobody publishes any Necromancer build for 3.2.0 at all. The argument is narrow and mechanical. 3.2.0's only real gift to Necromancer is the core-stat scalar going from 1.25 to 1.625, a flat 30% on baseline damage per 10 Intelligence. A scalar buff is worth most to the build that can actually spend its affix budget on the core stat - and the class's meta build cannot, because Blood Wave as a Core skill is resource-hungry enough that its published gearing is dominated by Essence Regeneration, Resource Cost Reduction and Lucky Hit restore tempers. Blood Lance is already in that build, as the Overpower-stack spender, and it is not the thing eating the resource budget. This page asks what happens if it is promoted from spender to carry. There is one piece of outside evidence, and it is Season 14 rather than 3.2.0: InfinityBuilds' 2026-08-02 list carries a Blood Lance Necromancer in A tier, titled 'Core Blood Tide Pit 139/Tower 134'. That is a real person clearing real content with the archetype on the live patch - it is not evidence about 3.2.0 and it is not a build guide this page could read, because the site's build pages are JavaScript-rendered.

Rotation
  1. Blood Lance held down as the main cast, Blood Wave on the Overpower cycle, Sever and Blood Mist to move, Bone Prison on anything tanky.
  2. Open on a small pull to build Resolve before engaging anything large.
Variants

Leveling — [ptr] Blood Lance from range as the main cast, Blood Wave when Overpower needs regaining, Sever and Blood Mist to move, Bone Prison on anything tanky. Watch Essence: the whole hypothesis is that this bar does not drain it the way the meta bar does.
Move on when [ptr] Level 70 and Torment 1 - or, on the PTR, whenever Mrak hands them to you - and a first Essence-per-second reading taken.

Early Endgame — [ptr] Blood Lance held down, Blood Wave on the Overpower cycle, everything else as before. This is where the two measurements get taken: Essence per second, and damage before and after stacking Intelligence.
Move on when [ptr] Essence measurably cheaper than the meta bar and Intelligence visibly converting. If either fails, stop.

Late Endgame — [ptr] Unchanged. Run the head-to-head against necromancer-meta-blood-wave here.
Move on when [ptr] The head-to-head is done and this build is at least competitive on packs.

Pushing — [ptr] Untested at push tiers by definition, and doubly provisional because it is PTR data. Open on a small pull to build Resolve before engaging anything large. Both 3.2.0 class tier reads still put Necromancer at the bottom of the game, so a good result here would be surprising and should be double-checked before it is believed.

Carried here on much weaker grounds than in the meta build - it doubles Blood Wave's wave, and this build barely casts Blood Wave. It is the first slot to re-examine. Where →

Reasoning

Hypothesis[ptr] A 30% core-stat scalar buff is worth more to a build that can afford to gear for the core stat. Blood Wave converts the 3.2.0 Necromancer scalar poorly because its own resource cost forces Essence Regeneration, Resource Cost Reduction and Lucky Hit restore rolls into most of its contested affix slots - the published gates are over 15 Essence Regeneration and over 25% Resource Cost Reduction before Ring of Starless Skies. Blood Lance sits in the same build already, costs less to cast, and is not what the resource gates were written for. Promoting it to the carry skill should free most of the jewelry budget for Intelligence and multipliers, which is exactly where a +30% scalar pays.
Confidencemedium
How to test it[ptr] (1) Measure Essence per second spent with Blood Lance as the carry versus Blood Wave as the carry, on the same character. The whole argument is that the first number is much smaller; if it is not, there is no freed budget and no build. (2) With the budget freed, stack Intelligence and re-measure damage - the 1.25 to 1.625 scalar is additive baseline damage, so it should show up as a clean percentage and can be checked rather than assumed. (3) Blood Lance is the Overpower *spender* in the meta build's loop; check what happens to the Bloodbath legendary node and the Dominate glyph when it becomes the spender and the gainer at once, because that loop was designed around two skills and this build has one. (4) Compare against necromancer-meta-blood-wave on the PTR at equal gear, on packs and on a single target. (5) Re-check everything at launch: 3.2.0 is a test build and the scalar is exactly the kind of number that moves between PTR and release.

Flame Surge

Core skillAldkin

Cooldown: 11 seconds

Fate: Aflame

Basic Attack: Fire Shot

Aldkin channels a cone of flame for 4 seconds, repeatedly dealing 80% Fire damage.

Aldkin's Mercenary Core Skill alters his Fate and Basic Attack.

Aldkin hurls a flaming bolt at an enemy, dealing 90% Fire damage and 55% Burning damage over 4 seconds.

Haunt

Core skillAldkin

Cooldown: 14 seconds

Fate: Forsaken

Basic Attack: Shadow Strike

Aldkin emits 3 ghostly souls at enemies, each Haunting their victims and dealing 90% Shadow damage over 10 seconds. If a target dies while being Haunted, its soul jumps to another target.

Aldkin's Mercenary Core Skill alters his Fate and Basic Attack.

Aldkin shoots a burst of shadow bolts at an enemy, each dealing 30% Shadow damage.

Storm of Fire

Iconic skillAldkin

Cooldown: 20 seconds

Aldkin rains a Fire Storm down from the sky that deals 300% Fire damage on impact and remains on the ground for 10 seconds. Every second, the Fire Storm Burns enemies within for 55% damage over 2.5 seconds.

Enemies hit by Fire Storm's impact or aftershocks have a 30% chance to be Stunned for 1.0 seconds.

Wave of Flame

Iconic skillAldkin

Cooldown: 25 seconds

Aldkin conjures a mass of flames forward, repeatedly dealing 550% Fire damage, Knocking Back enemies, and destroying small missiles.

Field of Languish

Iconic skillAldkin

Cooldown: 20 seconds

Aldkin desiccates an area for 6 seconds, Slowing enemies within by 40% and reducing their damage dealt by 20%.

Chain of Souls

Iconic skillAldkin

Cooldown: 21 seconds

Aldkin chains up to 10 enemies to himself, Tethering to them and dealing 84% Shadow damage over 2.5 seconds.

When the chains expire, they deal 35% Shadow damage and Stun their victims for 2.5 seconds.

Terrify

PassiveAldkin

Hits of Aldkin's Haunt have a 30% chance to inflict Vulnerable on enemies for 4 seconds.

Exhaustion

PassiveAldkin

Aldkin's Shadow damage has a 10% chance to Daze enemies for 2 seconds.

Paranoia

PassiveAldkin

Lucky Hit: Attacks against Languishing enemies have up to a 20% chance to Daze them for 1.0 seconds.

Languishing enemies take 15%[x] increased damage from you.

Condemned

PassiveAldkin

You instantly kill Languishing enemies with less than 40% Life. Does not work on Elites.

Shared Pain

PassiveAldkin

Aldkin's Chain of Souls Cooldown is reduced by 1.5 seconds when a chained target dies.

Amplified Suffering

PassiveAldkin

Damaging a Soul Chained enemy detonates the chain early, dealing 50% Shadow damage around them.

Covered in Ash

PassiveAldkin

Hits of Aldkin's Flame Surge Slow enemies by 20% and deal an additional 60% Burning damage over 3 seconds.

Raging Violence

PassiveAldkin

Allies gain 15%[+] Critical Strike Chance against enemies affected by Flame Surge.

Ember's Gift

PassiveAldkin

You restore 33 Resource per second while inside Aldkin's Fire Storm.

Eradication

PassiveAldkin

Enemies killed within Aldkin's Fire Storm explode for heavy Fire damage.

Raging Havoc

PassiveAldkin

Enemies damaged by Aldkin's Wave of Flame take 15%[x] increased Damage Over Time for 4 seconds.

Burning Chaos

PassiveAldkin

Aldkin's Wave of Flame Cooldown resets when you cast an Ultimate Skill.
